title: Cohort transfer rates - weekly tuning & standup notes (Sep 13-14, 2026)
content:
Attendees: Asha, Diego, Lena, Samir, Evan (ops drop-in)

Goal: quick sync on cohort transfer rate regressions we saw last week + decide next small experiments for KV cache sharding and micro-batching heuristics. Keep this as tactical notes and action list.

TL;DR:
- Observed 12% drop in KV hit rate for p50-prefill cohort on Sept 10–11 after the kernel change that introduced the short-circuit path (RD-4821).
- Median request batch size decreased from 6 -> 4 for that cohort causing higher per-token latency.
- Repro on staging with traffic replay: confirmed behavior when kernel handshake falls back to thin-state due to transient memory pressure.
- Quick mitigation: revert handshake heuristic in canary (defer for 24h), and test two config knobs (cohort-transfer-threshold, prefill-grace-window).

Recent metrics (prod, cohort p50, last 72h):
- KV hit rate: 0.72 -> 0.60 (drop on 2026-09-10 03:00 UTC)
- Median batch size: 6 -> 4
- p95 token-latency: 210ms -> 280ms
- CPU/GPU telemetry: small bump in kernel context switches, memory transient spikes on host-7 (investigate allocation churn)

Notes & hypotheses: 
1) Transfer window shrink due to handshake change: the new early-fallthrough path allowed some requests to bypass prefill; these requests then avoid KV warming -> smaller batches and miss more.
2) Backpressure interplay: when memory pressure kicks in, we drop prefill coalescing which hits small cohorts harder.
3) Cohort sampler skew: a small subset of client keys started routing differently after sampler tweak in RD-4999; increases cold-start frequency for those keys.

Experiments run this week (results):
- canary-rc: kernel handshake revert (small): rolled to 10% traffic in us-west; KV hit recovered to 0.68 over 6h, batch size climbed to 5. Partial improvement but not full.
- prefill-grace-window +50ms: staging run showed 3% hit improvement but increased median latency by 10ms for warm requests. Tradeoff acceptable? discuss.
- cohort-transfer-threshold tweak (from 0.2 -> 0.35): reduced transfer frequency but saw increased variance in batch sizes.

Decisions made:
- Revert handshake heuristic in canary for another full day and collect 48h metrics (Asha).
- Keep prefill-grace-window experiment running on staging; gather per-client latency histograms and compare tail impact (Diego + Lena).
- Pause cohort-sampler rollout (RD-4999) until we understand transfer behavior (Samir to coordinate with release-engineering).

Action items: 
- Asha: widen canary revert to 25% if metrics continue to improve; post update by 2026-09-14 EOD.
- Diego: add per-client KV hit annotation to telemetry (small dashboard tile) and instrument for top-10 skewed keys by tomorrow. (2026-09-14)
- Lena: run synthetic replay targeting host-7 allocation pattern and capture profiler outputs; estimate root cause of memory spikes (2026-09-16).
- Samir: hold RD-4999 merge; open a follow-up PR that includes a sampling rollback flag. (JIRA RD-5033)
- Evan: ops to watch host-7 during canary expansion and flag any OOMs; thumbs-up required for +25% canary.

Open questions / parking lot: 
- Is the memory pressure on host-7 systemic (allocation pattern) or ephemeral (worker GC)? Need flamegraphs.
- Should we bias prefill to prefer larger cohorts to protect throughput at cost of slight latency increase for tiny cohorts? Tradeoffs need numbers.
- Could we add a lightweight predictive sampler that detects cohort cold runs and forces prefill proactively? (spec sketch needed).

Notes to self / raw thoughts: 
- Some logs show repeated tiny batches from same client within 300ms window; might be client-side retry pattern + rehydration race. Add instrumentation for request origin and retry headers.
- Investigate whether quantization kernel path increases allocation churn when load is below 10k rps per host.

Useful links & commands (for quick reproduction):
- staging replay: k8s job: tools/replay/run_replay.sh --trace=2026-09-10-cohort-p50 --rate=1x
- profiler: perf record -e cpu-clock -p <pid> -- sleep 30 && perf script | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
- dashboard: /dashboards/serving/runtime/kv-hit-by-cohort

Meeting cadence: weekly tactical until transfer-rate stabilizes; next sync Tue 2026-09-21 09:30 PT (tentative).

Appendix (raw snippets):
- Snippet of log showing early fallthrough: 
  [2026-09-10T03:14:02Z] kernel: handshake: short-circuit=true, prefill-scheduled=false, cohort_id=us-east-3-78
  [2026-09-10T03:14:02Z] kv: miss client_id=abc123, reason=not_warmed

- Quick checklist before expanding revert to 25%:
  - confirm no OOM on canary hosts (Evan)
  - validate telemetry backfill includes top-5 keys (Diego)
  - smoke test end-to-end with function-calls workload (Lena)

If you have more data (trace ids, host ids) drop them here. This doc is a working scratchpad — expect shorthands and follow-ups.

-- Asha
